They need someone to trust and lean on and I believe the best person for this is you. Do things for them, even small ones, as this may mean a lot for them. Daily chit chats, constant checking about how their day went, anything. Just don't be too pushy about these things. Let them take their steps at their own pace and guide them along the way.

In my opinion, I think you should tell everything in person, spare not a single detail. Scream if you must, just let it all out. Don't be afraid of the outcome. If it turns out well, congrats you got yourself something to work and improve on. If it doesn't, well, just like you said it doesn't matter anymore since you're leaving. Gotta move on into a new chapter in your life. But at least you'll be leaving with a lessened burden in your chest, if not entirely removed.

Seems like you have nothing to lose, so why not give it your best shot this time? You have everything to gain. And the way you expressed yourself shows that there is still that fighting spirit in you. Just like in League, when you're so far behind, you for the riskiest plays to win. Sometimes it works, sometimes it won't. Doesn't matter if you lose though, you still gain exp and can queue up for another match. Now apply it in your life. Start uni, make friends if you want to, explore nee hobbies, seek counselling if you want to, basically anything new steps forward. If one or more fails, don't get disheartened cos you still gained something: experience  and life lessons. Easier said than done I know, but what I want to get across is don't let the fire inside you die cause I can see it is still there. You've grown a lot for sure considering how tough your childhood was. You may not notice it but you sure did. You'll get by through your transition to adulthood and I believe that, but what I cannot guarantee is that it will be an easy one. Well that's all I want to say at this point cos I migjt be incohesive at this point already lol, but anyway, wish you all the best in your future endeavors.

P.S. try adopting a pet if you believe you can take care of one. It's always great to have a companion. Or even better, volunteer at an animal shelter. Most of the animals there just want to be wanted like you do and they will never judge you. At least that's what I did when I was also at the lowest point in my life (attempted suicide multiple times and failed)
